timing: steady_clock per-operation user-space duration; includes clock, assertions, and allocation-hook overhead
allocation_scope: linker-wrapped direct malloc and overridden C++ new; excludes shared-library internal allocations and aligned new
pmu_scope: separate diagnostic run; whole-process aggregate counters include validation, setup, warmups, measured cases, and output/harness work; not attributed per case

reference_boundaries.shape_local_fill_enumerate: test-only shape-sized RefSlot array; reset, fill, and scan S slots for K present values. No formatting, frame encoding, schema validation, or public API.
reference_boundaries.full_schema_dense_fill_enumerate: test-only array with N equal to full FIX44 field count (912); reset/fill/scan all N slots for the same synthetic payload. It is a dense cost reference, not a competing implementation.
reference_boundaries.active_index_sparse_fill_enumerate: test-only K-slot payload plus sorted active indexes; includes descending insertion/sort work and scans K active entries. No formatting or validation.
reference_boundaries.direct_bounded_ordered_writer: complete wire writer for one fixed seven-field NewOrderSingle layout; checks output bounds and is byte-compared to generated encoder, but intentionally omits runtime schema/type/enum/required-field validation. Not an equivalent-speedup claim.
reference_boundaries.same_payload_comparison: the fixed NewOrderSingle payload with tags 11,21,55,54,60,38,40 is also fed to shape-local, N=912 dense, and active-index references. Those three rows measure fill/enumeration only; the direct writer measures complete framing and checksum.
reference_boundaries.generated_build_encode: generated FIX44 NewOrderSingle typed builder plus production encoder, including ordinary validation and complete frame formatting.
reference_boundaries.dynamic_runtime_tags_build_encode: explicit DynamicMessage construction with seven runtime tags, owned values, and production frame encoding; byte-compared with generated NewOrderSingle, but no dictionary enum/required-field validation. Reports its own heap allocation cost.
reference_boundaries.dynamic_prebuilt_encode_only: production encoding of a previously built DynamicMessage; excludes initial runtime plan/value allocation and does not include schema validation.
reference_boundaries.typed_parse_strict: inspect/flat parse, strict full-schema validation, and generated typed getters.
reference_boundaries.group_roundtrip: generated ExecutionReport and owned PartyIDs group build, production encode, parse, strict validation, and typed group projection.

validation_before_timing: generated direct writer output byte-for-byte equals production encoder for the fixed NewOrderSingle payload
direct writer and production encoder both reject too-small output spans
production encoder rejects missing required fields and an invalid Side enum
production frame parser rejects a changed checksum
each synthetic reference field sequence matches the fields parsed from production encoder output
group roundtrip verifies three PartyIDs and strict FIX44 schema validation

workload.rotating_case: generated NewOrderSingle IDs and quantities rotated over the configured input working set
workload.dense_N: full FIX44 field_count (912) in each synthetic dense-reference case

limitations: slot references are intentionally simple test-only candidates and do not reproduce production ownership or validation
benchmark numbers are local user-space costs, not end-to-end session/network latency
shape matrix uses synthetic tags 1000+index and generic string values; its encoder wire is only an equivalence oracle for ordering and field preservation

clang_template_instantiation_proxy.boundary: one small FIX44 consumer translation unit; compiler trace events are an instantiation proxy, not a compiler-independent template count

perf_event.scope: whole-benchmark aggregate from a separate diagnostic run; includes validation, setup, warmups, measured cases, and CSV/diagnostic harness; not per-case attribution

counters.scope: user-space phase-wide PMU diagnostics; existing threads plus inherited producers; includes harness; multiplex-scaled per-thread sums
